title: The plow, the hill and the bus at six
author: Ines Calder
standfirst: A winter night on Route 12, told hill by hill, from the salt yard to the first bus.
pull: If you wake up and the road is black, he did it right.
summary: The companion feature to episode 19, early for members.
body:
At ten past ten the salt yard at North Yard is lit like a stadium. Hal Brekke climbs into the cab of plow 12 and puts his coffee in the cup holder he fitted himself.

By midnight he has done Cobbler Hill twice. By four, the route card on his dashboard has a tick next to every street.

title: Night shelter, bed 31
author: Odile Varga
standfirst: A volunteer who has worked the winter shelter's overnight desk for seven years.
pull: You are not there to fix anyone. You are there to be awake.
summary: An interview from the winter issue, early for members.
body: The shelter on Tanner's Row opens at nine and takes its last guest at midnight. Then it is just the overnight desk, a kettle, and thirty-two beds.

title: Morrow's at four
author: Ines Calder
standfirst: Twenty years of bread on Corran Street, and the night it nearly ended.
pull: The bread does not care that it is the middle of the night.
summary: The cover story: a night at Morrow's bakery, from the alarm at midnight to the door at seven.
body:
The first thing you notice at Morrow's at one in the morning is that it is warm. The oven has been on since half past eleven, and the windows on Corran Street are fogged from the inside.

Dellah Morrow is already at the bench. She does not say hello. She hands you an apron.

In 2019 the oven broke at two in the morning, two days before Christmas. What happened next is why the street still has a bakery.

title: The bell at Saltgate
author: Kofi Lindahl
standfirst: Twelve photographs from the market floor between two and six.
pull: Nobody poses at four in the morning.
summary: A photo essay from Saltgate Fish Market, with captions by the porters.
body: Kofi Lindahl spent four nights on the market floor with a camera and no flash. These are the twelve frames the porters liked best.

title: What you eat at 4 a.m.
author: Mara Quint
standfirst: Every guest this season told us what they eat at four in the morning. We wrote it down.
summary: Field notes: the 4 a.m. meal, from eight night workers.
body: Agnes eats soup from a flask. Rafe eats whatever is left in the van. Soledad eats from the breakfast buffet before the guests do, which she says is the only perk of the job.

title: The swing bridge log, 1931 to now
author: Tobiah Rendle
standfirst: Ninety-five years of a bridge tender's ledger, read from the first page.
summary: An essay on the Ash Canal bridge ledger and the people who wrote in it.
body: The ledger in the Ash Canal bridge house has 31 volumes. Each line is a time, a vessel, and a name. Some lines are more than that.

title: Four on, four off
author: Odile Varga
standfirst: Night workers and their families on the shift pattern that runs their lives.
pull: My kids think Thursday is the weekend.
summary: A members-only interview with three families who live by a four-on, four-off rota.
body: Four nights on, four nights off. It sounds simple until you try to book a dentist.

title: A night at the front desk
author: Mara Quint
standfirst: Soledad Fuentes's notebook from one audit night, annotated.
pull: 3:12. Room 214 wants to know if the pool is open.
summary: Members-only field notes from the hotel night audit.
body: Soledad lent us the notebook she keeps under the front desk. We have reproduced one night of it, with her notes in the margin.

title: The last milk float
author: Ines Calder
standfirst: Ted Ayre's round, 340 doorsteps and the notes in the bottles.
summary: Feature from the summer issue: the last electric milk round in Corran.
body: The float hums. That is the only sound on Hollowmere Road at four, apart from the bottles.

title: The station rank
author: Kofi Lindahl
standfirst: Taxi drivers at Corran Central between the last two trains.
summary: Members-only photo essay from the summer issue.
body: Ten cabs, one train, and about forty people who need to get home.

title: Six hours of dark
author: Tobiah Rendle
standfirst: The shortest night of the year, spent with five people working through it.
pull: At midsummer the night is a rumor.
summary: Members-only essay from the summer issue.
body: On the twentieth of June the sun set at 9:31 and rose at 4:42. We spent every minute of the dark with someone at work.

title: Plates at eleven
author: Ines Calder
standfirst: The Herald's print works on the night of a late change.
pull: Stop the press, swap the plate, go again.
summary: From the archive: our first cover story, for members.
body: The paper goes to bed at eleven. Bernard Okoye's night is just starting.

title: The night bus atlas
author: Mara Quint
standfirst: Every night bus in Corran, ridden end to end in one week.
pull: The N4 has a regular who knits.
summary: From the archive: field notes on the night buses, for members.
